I am old, my back hurts, but I still work the land like I always did. Let me think how I will do this year, same way I been doing.

My 12 mu — I split it like always. About 8 mu I do wheat then maize same land, the double crop like everyone in our village. The other 4 mu I keep for cotton, because cotton bring cash money and my daughter-in-law help me with the picking.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant the same seed my neighbor Wang give me last autumn, improved kind, everyone around here use it. I put down 2 bag of compound fertilizer before ploughing — that's one bag for every 2 mu, maybe little more. Then when wheat turn green in spring I spread 1 bag urea for every 2 mu. So my nitrogen, altogether, is what you get from those bags. I water 3 times — once after planting, once at jointing, once when grain filling. If I don't water, wheat die, simple as that. I spray 2 time for aphid and the rust disease. Tractor man come plough for me, 40 yuan per mu, I pay him.

**Maize (summer):** After wheat cut, I just scatter seed in the stubble, no ploughing, save money and time. Seed is hybrid one from the dealer in town — everyone buy this one. I put 1 bag compound at sowing, then 2 bag urea when it reach my knee. That's what my son say to do, same as neighbor. Water maybe 2 time if rain not come. Spray once for the borer worm.

**Cotton (spring):** Cotton I been growing my whole life. I use the seed left from last year plus buy little new. I put 1 and half bag compound fertilizer per mu before planting — cotton eat a lot. Then topdress urea when it flower. I water 3 or 4 time, cotton need water. Spray many times, maybe 5 or 6, because bollworm and aphid always come. I plough proper with tractor, cotton need loose soil.

I spend maybe too much on fertilizer some say, but I rather have full wheat head than save few yuan and cry at harvest. My whole life I do it this way.
